inspection_summary: Inspected all 2,515 Python-split lines of the normalized source. The body combines a broad RH survey with a distinct finite-prime Weil-form/prolate-operator research program. Units preserve the paper's separation among proved background, reported computation, conditional constructions, asymptotic spectral matches, and the two explicitly unresolved gates. Formula-heavy passages were accepted only where checked prose recovers their semantic role; the extracted plots were not treated as quantitative evidence.

accepted_units.title: Equivalent formulations as a strategic black hole
accepted_units.why_material: The source distinguishes mathematically exact equivalence from proof-fertile reformulation and warns that a large catalog of equivalents can redirect effort without exposing a mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: The Redheffer example and subsequent logical discussion motivate the warning; the claim is strategic, not a theorem that equivalences are useless.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose and the sample determinant criterion are legible.

accepted_units.title: Finite-prime Weil forms joined to infrared and ultraviolet prolate models
accepted_units.why_material: The introduction isolates the paper's central proposed synthesis: finite-prime extremizers approximate low zeros, while a prolate operator also models high-energy zero behavior, with the trace formula connecting both roles.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a programmatic overview; later sections separate proved ingredients, numerical evidence, and missing convergence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: quotient and operator notation is fragmented in extraction, but the prose fixes the roles.

accepted_units.title: From prime-counting error to phase-doubling nonvanishing
accepted_units.why_material: The passage relates the strength of prime-counting error terms to zero location and gives the reusable phase-doubling contradiction behind nonvanishing on the line Re(s)=1.
accepted_units.context_note: The asymptotic formulas provide setup; the conceptual move is that phases accumulating near -1 square to phases near +1, forcing an impossible extra pole.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: displayed asymptotics are readable enough with surrounding prose.

accepted_units.title: Tauberian mediation and the elementary PNT contrast
accepted_units.why_material: It explains how Tauberian theorems expose the analytic-input-to-arithmetic-output bridge and contrasts that conceptual reorganization with the later proof that complex analysis is not logically necessary.
accepted_units.context_note: The detailed Wiener-Ikehara mechanism appears in lines 2093-2110 and is separately retained.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose and the Selberg symmetry formula are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: The correct variable in Riemann's conditionally convergent zero sum
accepted_units.why_material: The text shows why Li(x^rho) suppresses branch data and why Ei(rho log x) preserves the variable needed for a meaningful conditionally convergent explicit formula.
accepted_units.context_note: This corrects notation rather than changing the underlying explicit-formula theorem; lines 2182-2204 give the expanded formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: branch-integral cases are layout-fragmented, but the prose makes the representation defect and repair unambiguous.

accepted_units.title: Explicit formula as a zeros-versus-places distribution identity
accepted_units.why_material: The Guinand-Weil form replaces a pointwise prime-counting expression by a test-function identity whose Mellin transforms sample zeros and whose local distributions decompose over all places.
accepted_units.context_note: Compact support is the later key to retaining only finitely many prime contributions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: formulas are fragmented across lines but symbols and prose jointly recover the construction.

accepted_units.title: Gaussian smoothing reveals hidden prime-counting sign changes
accepted_units.why_material: The passage identifies Gaussian averaging of the explicit formula as the mechanism that converted an enormous ineffective-looking crossing scale into tractable localization of sign changes.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical numerical bounds are evidence of method refinement, not an RH proof route by themselves.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: the prose is clear; one very large displayed bound has degraded exponent layout.

accepted_units.title: Hardy's real Z-function converts critical-line zeros into sign changes
accepted_units.why_material: Choosing the phase so Z(t) is real turns critical-line zero detection into a real-variable sign-change problem, with the approximate functional equation supplying analyzable oscillatory structure.
accepted_units.context_note: This establishes infinitely many critical-line zeros, not a positive proportion or RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the phase formula is split, but the mechanism is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Mollification upgrades infinitude to a positive proportion
accepted_units.why_material: Selberg's mollifier controls zeta on average and changes the target from isolated sign changes to a quantitative lower bound N0(T) comparable with T log T; later refinements optimize the same mechanism.
accepted_units.context_note: The detailed mollifier form is supplied in lines 2111-2119; percentage records do not approach a proof that all zeros lie on the line.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose is clear and quantitative statements are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Zero-density control versus Lindelöf convexity control
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts counting zeros in right half-strips with controlling zeta growth on vertical lines, and shows how the functional equation plus convexity propagates the Lindelöf boundary value.
accepted_units.context_note: Lindelöf is stated as weaker than RH; zero-density improvements remain partial distributional information.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: one density exponent is visually fragmented, but the conceptual comparison is prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Evenness compresses the Hadamard product for Xi
accepted_units.why_material: Completing zeta produces an order-one entire function, and the functional equation makes Xi even so paired zeros cancel exponential factors and yield a product in squared zero parameters.
accepted_units.context_note: The source also distinguishes xi(0) from Xi(0), explaining a normalization typo in Riemann's formula.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: product notation is split but its pairing logic is explicitly stated.

accepted_units.title: Jensen's boundary average becomes Nevanlinna value distribution
accepted_units.why_material: The passage reframes Jensen's balance between boundary growth and interior zeros/poles as the prototype for Nevanlinna characteristic and a-point distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: It reports that direct Nevanlinna applications have not proved RH and uses the theory mainly to contextualize the exceptional value zero.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the Jensen formula is legible with prose.

accepted_units.title: Critical-line alignment is unstable under nonzero additive perturbation
accepted_units.why_material: Borchsenius-Jessen is used as an adversarial contrast: for every nonzero x, solutions of zeta(s)=x crowd the strip immediately to the right of the critical line, making x=0 exceptional.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem concerns a-points and limiting distributions; it neither proves nor refutes RH for zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: enumerated consequences and interpretation are clear.

accepted_units.title: Universality from phase choices in a Hilbert-space dense-series theorem
accepted_units.why_material: Voronin approximation is reduced to a reusable functional-analytic mechanism: square-summable vectors with divergent projections admit dense convergent unit-phase sums, applied to logarithms of Euler factors.
accepted_units.context_note: The approximated targets must be nonvanishing on suitable compacta; universality does not itself locate zeta zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the Hilbert-space conditions are recoverable despite formula line breaks.

accepted_units.title: Self-adjoint eigenvalues and scattering resonances as competing zero models
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates the direct Hilbert-Polya template, where reality follows from self-adjointness, from scattering models where zeros appear as resonances and boundary conditions remain unresolved.
accepted_units.context_note: Statistical resemblance to quantum chaos does not supply the missing rigorous operator.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose is self-contained.

accepted_units.title: Geometric RH from intersection pairing to Frobenius cohomology
accepted_units.why_material: The function-field analogue shows two successive representations of RH-type control: positivity of an intersection pairing and absolute values of Frobenius eigenvalues in etale cohomology.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a proved finite-characteristic model and an analogy for the arithmetic case, not a transfer theorem for classical RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: cohomology subscripts and determinant products are partially degraded, but the prose states the map.

accepted_units.title: Primes as knots through the etale fundamental group
accepted_units.why_material: The Mumford-Mazur analogy reframes prime interaction as linking data in covers, with the etale fundamental group supplying the covering-space language.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a conceptual analogy elaborated later by the adele-class mapping-torus construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose is clear.

accepted_units.title: Motives as a universal carrier for zeta and L-function structure
accepted_units.why_material: Motives are presented as a compression across cohomology theories that would make analytic properties consequences of geometric structure.
accepted_units.context_note: Mixed motives and the desired classical cohomological interpretation remain conjectural.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose only.

accepted_units.title: Adeles connect global-field arithmetic, harmonic analysis, and Langlands transfer
accepted_units.why_material: Passing from a discrete global field to its locally compact adele ring creates harmonic-analytic structure; Langlands then proposes equality between motivic and automorphic L-functions.
accepted_units.context_note: The general Langlands correspondences and generalized RH remain open, so the bridge supplies organization rather than a proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose is clear.

accepted_units.title: Ramanujan-Petersson as RH at Euler-factor scale
accepted_units.why_material: Modular-form L-functions provide concrete analytic continuation and functional equations, while the bound on local coefficients realizes an RH-like constraint at each Euler factor.
accepted_units.context_note: The example clarifies expected structure for broader L-functions but does not imply classical RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the series display is fragmented but prose and bound are clear.

accepted_units.title: The sign mismatch between Selberg and Riemann explicit formulas
accepted_units.why_material: The Selberg trace formula gives a complete geometric-spectral interpretation, yet its prime/geodesic terms occur with the opposite sign from the Riemann explicit formula, isolating a structural obstruction to naive transfer.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison is analogical and sign-sensitive; matching Euler products and functional equations is insufficient.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: displayed sums are split, but the sign contrast is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Local unfolding enables GUE comparison but obstructs a fixed global operator
accepted_units.why_material: Zero spacings agree with GUE only after a height-dependent rescaling that compensates for logarithmically increasing density; the source infers that the correspondence is inherently local rather than the spectrum of a simple fixed ensemble.
accepted_units.context_note: This concerns local statistics and does not rule out every self-adjoint spectral realization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: density and rescaling formulas are recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Family symmetry selects unitary, orthogonal, or symplectic zero statistics
accepted_units.why_material: Katz-Sarnak turns one numerical analogy into a family-level classification where arithmetic structure determines the random-matrix symmetry type, proved in finite-field families via Frobenius equidistribution.
accepted_units.context_note: Classical number-field predictions remain conjectural in the stated regime.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: prose is self-contained.

accepted_units.title: Zeta moments split into universal matrix and arithmetic Euler factors
accepted_units.why_material: The Keating-Snaith model separates the moment constant into a universal determinant-moment factor and a zeta-specific Euler product, a reusable universal-versus-arithmetic decomposition.
accepted_units.context_note: Beyond the stated low moments, these constants are conjectural predictions rather than proved asymptotics.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: product formulas are readable with the bullet explanation.

accepted_units.title: Adele-class zeros as an absorption spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: The noncommutative adele-class quotient realizes zeros through a trace formula whose spectral side is an absorption spectrum, accounting for the negative sign absent from Selberg's model.
accepted_units.context_note: The semilocal formula is proved as reported, while a global RH-equivalent version must allow noncritical zeros and does not establish positivity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: cross-product and quotient notation is readable with prose.

accepted_units.title: Prime linking encoded by periodic-orbit mapping tori
accepted_units.why_material: A prime's periodic orbit in the adele-class sector lifts to a mapping torus whose monodromy records its linking with other primes, concretizing the primes-as-knots analogy in class-field-theoretic data.
accepted_units.context_note: One extraction control character appears in line 1119, but the surrounding theorem clauses recover the statement; this construction is not an RH proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: one corrupt character and dense etale notation require prose-led reading.

accepted_units.title: Numerical zero verification couples fast evaluation with rigorous counting
accepted_units.why_material: The computational history culminates in the reusable distinction between approximating zeros with the Riemann-Siegel/Odlyzko-Schonhage machinery and certifying completeness with error bounds and Turing's method.
accepted_units.context_note: Finite verification supplies strong evidence and tests exceptions but cannot establish an infinite statement.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: list and prose are clear.

accepted_units.title: Compact support localizes Weil positivity to finitely many primes
accepted_units.why_material: Weil's criterion turns RH into positivity of convolution test functions; compact multiplicative support forces all but finitely many local prime distributions to vanish at each scale.
accepted_units.context_note: The archimedean-only positivity result is numerical/limited and the source explicitly says it gives no conceptual extension once primes enter.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: several displayed formulas are layout-fragmented, but the finite-support mechanism and limitation are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Beurling-Nyman turns RH into an L2 density problem
accepted_units.why_material: The criterion changes a zero-location statement into completeness of constrained fractional-part functions, with approximation rate reflecting off-line zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The extraction of the summation notation is imperfect; the functional-analytic role is prose-recoverable.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: formula-dependent but intelligible.

accepted_units.title: Li coefficients turn RH into positivity of a sequence
accepted_units.why_material: Li's criterion compresses the zero multiset into scalar coefficients whose positivity for every index is equivalent to RH.
accepted_units.context_note: The source states the criterion without developing a proof mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: coefficient formula is split but recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Arithmetic equivalences expose decidability without supplying feasible proof search
accepted_units.why_material: Robin and Lagarias translate RH into universal divisor-sum inequalities, after which the source contrasts decidable instances with the cost of direct verification and speculates about provability limits.
accepted_units.context_note: The broad Chaitin/Godel discussion is the author's interpretation; syntactic universality and costly checking do not establish independence or unprovability.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: arithmetic criteria and prose are clear.

accepted_units.title: Finite-prime Weil quadratic form produces a real-zero Mellin transform
accepted_units.why_material: For functions supported in a finite multiplicative interval, only finitely many prime powers enter the explicit-formula quadratic form; a normalized minimizer is then mapped by Mellin transform to an entire function whose zeros lie on the critical line under a simplicity/evenness condition.
accepted_units.context_note: Existence and zero reality are conditional on the stated spectral property; the construction does not yet identify these zeros with zeta zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: convolution and Mellin notation is fragmented, but the construction chain is prose-explicit.

accepted_units.title: Extreme finite-prime agreement still leaves the convergence theorem open
accepted_units.why_material: The computed first fifty zeros from primes at most 13 closely match zeta zeros, motivating a limit in which minimizers converge and Hurwitz preserves line-supported zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The source explicitly labels convergence of the minimizers or their transforms as unproved; numerical improbability is not a proof and the error list is only reported evidence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low for the logical structure; the long numerical table is legible but not independently certified here.

accepted_units.title: Decompose the finite-to-infinite limit through Hermite and prolate approximants
accepted_units.why_material: The proposed route recenters the minimizer, represents Xi through a Hermite summation map, localizes the Hermite functions by prolate eigenfunctions, and separates approximant convergence from approximation of the true minimizer.
accepted_units.context_note: This roadmap anticipates the missing comparison and simplicity gates rather than resolving them.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: prose gives a complete dependency chain.

accepted_units.title: Simple even extremizers have Fourier transforms with only real zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Theorem 6.1 supplies the rigorous rigidity engine: a lower-bounded convolution-kernel operator with a simple isolated minimum and even eigenfunction yields an entire Fourier transform with all zeros real.
accepted_units.context_note: Application to the Weil minimizer requires verifying every spectral hypothesis; the proof is summarized via finite matrices and Hurwitz, not reproduced.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: theorem text is recoverable despite a broken hat accent.

accepted_units.title: Xi as the Fourier transform of a summed Hermite combination
accepted_units.why_material: Poisson summation and the map E express Riemann's Xi as the Fourier transform of E(h), where h is the unique zero-integral combination of two Fourier-invariant Hermite modes.
accepted_units.context_note: This identifies the intended limiting function but does not show finite Weil minimizers converge to it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: central formulas are extraction-fragmented, though Fact 6.2 states the representation in prose.

accepted_units.title: Prolate eigenfunctions jointly diagonalize time and band limitation
accepted_units.why_material: The commuting prolate differential operator resolves the angle between time-support and frequency-support projections, providing localized analogues of Hermite functions whose first relevant eigenvalues approach one exponentially.
accepted_units.context_note: The result supplies approximation geometry, not by itself a statement about Weil minimizers.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: projection notation is degraded, but commutation, simplicity, parity, and asymptotics are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: The smallest restricted-Weil eigenvalue tracks a prolate leakage eigenvalue
accepted_units.why_material: The restricted Weil form is represented by a compact-resolvent self-adjoint operator; numerics motivate E applied to a zero-integral combination of the first prolate modes as the smallest-eigenvector ansatz.
accepted_units.context_note: The comparison with the plotted angular eigenvalue and the eigenvector identification are reported numerical evidence, not the missing approximation theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: Figure 1 is not recoverable as data from text extraction, but the claimed correspondence and ansatz are stated in prose.

accepted_units.title: Poisson summation turns near time-frequency intersection into a near Weil radical
accepted_units.why_material: Because the global E-range lies in the Weil radical, simultaneous approximate time and band limitation creates compactly supported near-radical vectors; prolate modes quantify the failure of the two projection ranges to intersect exactly.
accepted_units.context_note: The mechanism motivates k_lambda but does not bound its distance from the actual minimum eigenvector theta_x.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: projection symbols are partially garbled, while support implications and obstruction are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Prolate-Hermite approximants converge to Xi on closed substrips
accepted_units.why_material: Classical prolate-to-Hermite estimates yield uniform-on-closed-substrip convergence of the Fourier transforms of k_lambda to Xi, providing the analytic convergence side needed for a Hurwitz argument.
accepted_units.context_note: This convergence concerns the constructed k_lambda, not the true Weil minimizers theta_x.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the strip and error-bound formula are fragmented but Fact 6.4 is clear.

accepted_units.title: Two unresolved gates separate the program from RH
accepted_units.why_material: The source names the exact remaining obligations: prove the restricted Weil minimum is simple with an even eigenvector, and prove the prolate ansatz sufficiently approximates that eigenvector.
accepted_units.context_note: Analogy with the prolate operator is evidence only; neither gate is claimed solved.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Low: concise prose.

accepted_units.title: Scaling kernels realize Frobenius correspondences as divisors
accepted_units.why_material: In the adelic scaling-site picture, Schwartz kernels mediate between operators and geometric correspondences, with the delta kernel of scaling representing the Frobenius divisor.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is a geometric framework for investigating Weil positivity, not an established positivity proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the kernel formula is legible.

accepted_units.title: Time and frequency cutoffs rewrite the archimedean local term
accepted_units.why_material: The archimedean trace formula uses independent support and bandwidth projections, turning the local Weil distribution into a trace identity in exactly the operators used in information theory.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the prime-free local bridge; the semilocal extension is separate.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: equation (19) is layout-fragmented, but its parameters and interpretation are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Sonin space supplies an archimedean positivity lower bound
accepted_units.why_material: Functions vanishing with their Fourier transforms on a common interval define the orthogonal complement of the two projection ranges, and compression to this Sonin space yields a positive trace lower bound for the archimedean Weil functional.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem has support and Fourier-vanishing restrictions and covers no finite-prime contribution.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: theorem notation is degraded but the inequality and space are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Semilocal adele quotients assemble into a cross-product sheaf
accepted_units.why_material: Finite sets of places define quotients A_S/Gamma_S whose Bruhat-Schwartz cross products form a sheaf over Spec Z; its generic stalk and global sections connect semilocal and global arithmetic geometry.
accepted_units.context_note: The source says the function space for the trace formula is best viewed through Hochschild homology; this is structural setup, not positivity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: products and subscripts are crowded but theorem clauses are readable.

accepted_units.title: The semilocal trace formula inserts finite-prime contributions into the projection identity
accepted_units.why_material: Equation (22) extends the archimedean time-band trace representation to a finite set of places, giving an operator-theoretic form of the restricted Weil quadratic form used in the minimizer comparison.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage presents this as a step toward explaining numerical eigenvector agreement, not as the needed quantitative comparison.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: the displayed trace formula is fragmented; surrounding prose fixes the correspondence.

accepted_units.title: Infrared determinant convergence and ultraviolet heat asymptotics are distinct targets
accepted_units.why_material: The spectral-triple viewpoint separates low eigenvalues, modeled by rank-one perturbations whose normalized determinants are intended to approach Xi, from high eigenvalues, modeled through heat asymptotics and a prolate operator.
accepted_units.context_note: The determinant convergence is described as potential work, and the heat model immediately assumes RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: prose is clear though operator superscripts are degraded.

accepted_units.title: The zeta-zero heat expansion is asymptotic and factorially divergent
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming RH and a self-adjoint operator with zeta ordinates as spectrum, the explicit formula gives a heat-trace expansion whose coefficient growth proves it is not convergent.
accepted_units.context_note: The operator is posited under RH; the expansion cannot be used here as an unconditional spectral construction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: coefficients are formula-heavy and fragmented, but the assumption and divergence conclusion are explicit.

accepted_units.title: A self-adjoint prolate extension matches ultraviolet zero asymptotics
accepted_units.why_material: Restricting the natural self-adjoint prolate extension to Sonin space yields discrete negative spectrum, and a Darboux-built Dirac square root has the same ultraviolet behavior as zeta zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: This is asymptotic spectral matching, not equality of individual spectra and not control of low zeros; the plotted proximity is not accepted as extra quantitative data.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: operator formulas are readable with prose; the following figure is omitted as extraction-defective.

accepted_units.title: Wiener-Ikehara converts boundary regularity into the PNT
accepted_units.why_material: The note makes the Tauberian bridge explicit: nonnegativity plus extension after pole subtraction converts analytic control of the logarithmic derivative into psi(x) asymptotic to x.
accepted_units.context_note: This elaborates c71_u004 and does not strengthen the zero-free input.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: the transform convention is extraction-fragmented but the implication is fully stated.

accepted_units.title: Nevanlinna growth and Borchsenius-Jessen limiting distribution
accepted_units.why_material: The notes define proximity and pole-counting terms, report zeta's characteristic growth, and state that the limiting distribution of log zeta has full complex support in the inner strip without assuming RH.
accepted_units.context_note: These details support the exceptional-value and instability unit; they are reported results rather than derived here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: several integrals are split, but definitions and conclusions are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Expanded Ei formula preserves branch-sensitive zero dependence
accepted_units.why_material: The note demonstrates the periodicity defect in x^beta and writes the corrected zero sum using Ei(rho log x), making the earlier representation repair explicit.
accepted_units.context_note: The passage critiques notation in one source; it does not claim the classical explicit formula itself is false.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: the final formula is fragmented but its replacement rule is explicit.

accepted_units.title: Angles between projections classify near intersections
accepted_units.why_material: The note explains that a pair of closed subspaces is classified componentwise by an angle satisfying P cos^2(alpha)=PQP, the abstraction used by the prolate construction.
accepted_units.context_note: This is supporting operator geometry; quantitative prolate concentration requires the earlier spectral facts.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: formula typography is compressed but readable.

accepted_units.title: The module identifies the semilocal quotient with the trace-formula Hilbert space
accepted_units.why_material: The semilocal module descends through the quotient, identifies additive and multiplicative L2 spaces, and reduces the general trace formula to the kernel-invariant component used in equation (22).
accepted_units.context_note: This is interface machinery for the semilocal formula, not an independent positivity result.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High-to-moderate: dense notation is partially degraded, but the map and specialization are stated.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Finite localization without finite sufficiency
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Compact support makes each Weil test depend on finitely many primes, and extremization yields line-rigid approximants; the global problem is displaced into controlling the scale limit rather than eliminated.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Neither finite-prime positivity nor the observed zero match proves simplicity or convergence as the support grows.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From prolate concentration to a candidate RH limit
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Time-frequency concentration constructs a near-radical vector whose Fourier transform has a proved Xi limit, while the real-zero theorem would transfer rigidity if it were identified with the true Weil minimizer.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The required minimizer simplicity/evenness and quantitative k_lambda-to-theta_x comparison remain open.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Information theory as the common operator language
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The same pair of support and bandwidth projections governs prolate concentration, Sonin-space positivity, and the archimedean-to-semilocal trace formulas.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: A shared operator vocabulary does not yet provide the finite-prime positivity or eigenvector bound needed for RH.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Infrared and ultraviolet are complementary but nonidentical spectral evidence
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Low-lying finite-prime approximants and high-energy prolate asymptotics probe different ends of a proposed zeta spectral geometry.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not construct one operator with the exact full zeta spectrum; the heat expansion is conditional and the UV match is asymptotic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Why the Riemann trace formula needs absorption
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The negative prime-side sign obstructing a direct Selberg analogy is reinterpreted by the adele-class trace formula as an absorption rather than emission spectrum.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This interpretation organizes the sign but does not establish Weil positivity.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Function-field transfer map and its arithmetic gap
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Intersection positivity, Frobenius cohomology, adeles, and Schwartz kernels outline successive representation changes by which a geometric RH proof might be imitated over Spec Z.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Each bridge remains analogical in the classical case; no arithmetic cohomology with the required positivity is produced.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Universality versus engineered zero rigidity
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Zeta's nonzero value behavior is extremely flexible, whereas Fourier transforms of simple even extremizers form a deliberately rigid class with real zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: These concern different function classes, so the contrast supplies design intuition rather than a direct implication about zeta.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Statistical universality separated from exact spectral realization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Random matrices explain unfolded local statistics and universal moment factors, while the prolate construction targets an operator-level ultraviolet asymptotic.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Local statistics, moment predictions, and ultraviolet matching are all weaker than equality with the exact zeta zero set.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Branch-aware representations as a correctness prerequisite
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Explicit formulas must retain rho log x rather than only x^rho because conditional summation depends on branch-sensitive information lost by exponentiation.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This repairs notation and interpretation but does not alter the unresolved zero-location problem.
